wv_ganja_bloc_aka_moon_board.blurb: A single large boulder tucked into Darkside East, part of Darnell Hollow in the University Research Forest near Cheat Canyon. It holds 18 problems and nearly every line on it is considered worth doing. The grades start around V2 and climb steeply from there: the bulk sit between V4 and V7, with a handful of hard problems in the V8 to V10 range, so it suits strong boulderers more than beginners. Names like Slopey Rail hint at the style, with plenty of rounded holds. Darnell Hollow has the most roadside bouldering in the forest and runs a few degrees warmer than the higher ground, which helps outside the summer heat.

wv_hole_n_the_wall.blurb: A quiet little cliff in Snake Hill Wildlife Management Area on the Cheat Canyon side of northern West Virginia. The rock is sandstone, and the wall is only about 30 to 40 feet tall. Of its 18 routes, twelve are bolted sport lines, three are top-ropes and three are trad. Grades run from easy 5.4 up to 5.12, with the largest group at 5.11, though there are a few moderate routes in the 5.7 to 5.9 range. It is a decent place to practice leading, and some of the boulders nearby have good problems. Bring quickdraws, a trad rack for setting top-ropes, and a pad if you want to boulder.

wv_riverbend.blurb: Riverbend is the smaller of the two climbing zones at Franklin Gorge, near Franklin in eastern West Virginia, found downstream from the main wall. All 18 routes are bolted sport climbs, and the grade spread leans hard: a couple of 5.9s and 5.10s, a few 5.11s, then mostly 5.12 with a few 5.13 lines at the top. The face mostly looks south and gets sun through the middle of the day during the high season, so summer afternoons can be hot. It is worth the trip for strong sport climbers, and it is a poor pick for anyone after a warm-up crag. The walk in is rough and overgrown rather than a tidy trail.

wv_0_zero_buttress.blurb: Zero Buttress is one of the buttresses of the Upper Meadow, upstream of the highway bridge on the Meadow River in the New River Gorge region. It faces south, so it is sunny, and some routes finish with a view of the bridge. Of its 17 routes, 16 are sport and one is trad. The grades are friendly to a broad crowd: a few lines in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, a big cluster at 5.10, and a handful at 5.11. That makes it a good pick for climbers working through the 5.10s on bolts. The cliff is sandstone, and it can be warm on sunny days.

wv_11_bubba_buttress.blurb: Bubba Buttress is the first crag you meet on the way into Bubba City, in the New River Gorge region. It has 17 routes, 11 sport and 6 trad, and the front face of the main buttress is regarded as excellent. Grades stretch from 5.6 to 5.13, but most of the weight is in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with a few easier lines in the 5.6 to 5.9 range. Several routes here earn three stars, making it a strong choice for climbers who are comfortable on steeper, sustained sandstone and want a mix of crack climbing and bolted faces. Beginners will find only a handful of options.

wv_satisfaction_wall_the.blurb: A long stretch of cliff at Summersville Lake, running between Long Wall and Narcissus Cave. It faces south, so expect plenty of sun, and it is rarely crowded. The 17 routes are a mix of 13 sport lines and 4 trad lines, with a lot of variety in style. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.11. One route is in the 5.6 range and three are at 5.9, but the core is 5.10 with a good dose of 5.11, so it is best for climbers who already lead in that range. The belay for some routes sits on the main trail, so share the space with passing climbers.

wv_boxcar_boulder.blurb: A pair of boulders just below the Cardinal Trail in the East Boulders section of Valley Falls State Park in northern West Virginia. Boxcar is the larger of the two. It holds 17 problems with railroad-themed names, spanning from V0 up to an unclimbed project at roughly V11 to V12. Most of the problems are easy to middling, with several in the V0 to V2 range and a middle group between V3 and V6. Two of the harder lines, Amtrak and Big Train, are the standouts. It is a reasonable choice for a mixed-ability group, though the approach is a hike of a good 20 minutes or more from the main parking area.

wv_contact_zone.blurb: Contact Zone is a section of the Main Wall at Franklin Gorge, near Franklin in eastern West Virginia, sitting uphill and upstream from the main parking area. It has 17 routes, 16 of them bolted sport lines and one trad. The grades run from 5.8 to 5.12, with the weight in the middle: four 5.9s, five 5.10s, three 5.11s, and four 5.12s. That gives it something for climbers moving from moderate bolted routes into harder terrain. Aloha, a 5.9, is the most-rated line, and the hardest classic here is a 5.12.
